name: applicationId
note: engine-id (8 bits) + selector (24 bits); CLI collect application name; exportable under v9 and IPFIX; engine ids per RFC 6759 section 4.1: 3 IANA-L4 (port based), 6 USER-Defined (custom), 13 PANA-L7 (NBAR2 layer 7)

name: applicationName
note: carried by option application-table, not in data records

name: HTTP Host
note: Cisco's guide gives the wire-level specifier 45003 = 0x8000 | 12235 (enterprise bit set); libfds gives the IE id 12235; same element; IPFIX only, max 512 chars IOS / 2 KB IOS XE; see NOTES.md; CAPTURE (c8000v-26.01.02-capture): the value is NOT a bare hostname but a constant 6-byte prefix 03 00 00 50 34 02 (applicationId http + sub-application id 0x3402) followed by the hostname, prefix alone when the record has no host, never empty, on all 1302 records regardless of the flow's own applicationId; nl6 emits exactly this since nl6#679 from the single constant avcHostPrefix in ipfix_avc.go, and the capture test compares the pcap against that constant

name: HTTP URI statistics
note: Cisco's guide gives the wire-level specifier 42125 = 0x8000 | 9357 (enterprise bit set); libfds gives the IE id 9357 (appHTTPUriStatistics); same element; type octetArray is an nl6 encoder decision, not a sourced fact: Cisco names no IPFIX type and libfds (the only stated type) says string, but the field embeds NUL bytes and binary counts, so IPFIX string semantics would be wrong; URI/count pairs repeat back to back: NUL(0x00)-delimited URI string then a 2-byte integer hit count, byte order not stated; IOS truncates URI at 512 chars, IOS XE caps the field at 2 KB; max hit count 65535; see NOTES.md; hit-count byte order is NOT stated by Cisco and is an encoder assumption unit 2 must decide before this field is emitted; CAPTURE (c8000v-26.01.02-capture): all 400 values are URI then NUL then a 2-byte BIG-ENDIAN count with NO trailing delimiter, exactly nl6's uriStatsValue output; the URI is the FIRST PATH SEGMENT only (/api/v1 arrives as /api); present only on the ingress-direction record of an http-classified request

name: connection id
note: CLI match connection id; a 32-bit per-connection identifier, 0 on ICMP flows; not a documented source but the capture shows IOS-XE 26.01.02 REFUSES to bind a monitor whose record collects URI statistics without it as a MATCH field, and refuses match connection id without cache timeout event transaction-end on the monitor; nl6 does not emit it, see nl6#680

name: applicationDescription
note: non-scope field of the application-table options template (RFC 6759 section 4.3); Cisco 2015 guide: offset 28, length 55 in option application-table; RFC 6759 section 7.1.1 registers it as Abstract Data Type string with no fixed length
